accessLogs.chSectionHint: An external ClickHouse server stores and analyzes logs. The panel only forwards data to it.
accessLogs.chPasswordHint: Leave blank to keep the current password.
accessLogs.chRequired: This feature needs ClickHouse. Configure the connection in Settings.
accessLogs.retentionHint: ClickHouse automatically deletes logs older than this period.
accessLogs.maskClientIpHint: When on, exact source-IP search is unavailable.
accessLogs.ingestUrlHint: Empty = derived from the panel address.
accessLogs.disabledBanner: Access-log collection is disabled. Enable it in Settings.
accessLogs.purgeConfirm: Delete all stored access logs? This cannot be undone.
accessLogs.usersByIpHint: Many distinct IPs for one user may indicate subscription sharing.
accessLogs.usersByFanoutHint: High unique-destination counts may indicate torrents or scanning.
accessLogs.usersByIpExpand: Click a user to see all their IPs.

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.ipAddressHelp: Server address used for SSH and panel service connections. It is also used in subscriptions when no suitable public domain or edge address is configured.
nodes.domainHelp: Hysteria: used for the ACME certificate and as the subscription address. Xray: used as the node address and, with ACME/Manual TLS, as the TLS serverName and HTTP Host.
nodes.sniHint: Custom client SNI without an ACME domain. The panel publishes it to clients, disables server sniGuard, and enables certificate verification bypass. It is ignored when a domain is set.
nodes.commentHint: Free-form note shown in the node list and dashboard (up to 500 characters)
nodes.portHelp: Hysteria: the main server UDP port, direct client port, and Port Hopping range redirect target. Xray: the main VLESS inbound and client connection port. Use 1–65535 without conflicts with other listeners.
nodes.portRangeHint: Celerity publishes this range to clients. A full SSH setup of a regular remote node can create UDP redirects to the main port; run node setup again after changing the range.
nodes.statsPortHelp: TCP port for Hysteria's Traffic Stats API. Celerity reaches it at the node IP for traffic, online-user and kick requests. Auto Setup opens it in the firewall; restrict access to the panel IP when possible.
nodes.statsSecretHelp: Secret carried in the Authorization header for the Traffic Stats API. Celerity needs it for API requests; without a secret, the generator omits trafficStats from the config.
nodes.sectionStatsHint: HTTP Traffic Stats API for Hysteria only; Xray statistics come through CC Agent.
nodes.groupsHint: Users of these groups will have access to this node. If not selected — available to all.
nodes.sshSettingsHint: Used by Auto Setup, synchronization, terminal, Caddy Front, init script, and SSH key management.
nodes.sshPrivateKeyHint: Paste your private key (OpenSSH or PEM format). Leave empty to keep current.
nodes.generateSshKeyHint: Generates an ed25519 keypair and installs the public key on the server via SSH (requires password or existing key).
nodes.generateSshKeyWarning:
Generate and install a new SSH key on this node?

This will:
• Generate a new ed25519 keypair
• Add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
• Save the private key to the panel (encrypted)

The existing password will remain unchanged.
nodes.downloadSshKeyMissing: SSH private key is not configured for this node
nodes.initScriptHint: Bash script run before the main Auto Setup with NODE_IP, NODE_NAME, NODE_TYPE, and NODE_DOMAIN. A script failure is logged but does not stop setup.
nodes.maxOnlineHint: 0 = unlimited. With global hideOverloaded, a real node is excluded at onlineUsers ≥ limit. Hysteria uses /online; Xray counts users with traffic in the latest Agent poll, not exact concurrent sessions. Virtual and CDN nodes have no local counter.
nodes.rankingHint: Lower means earlier among real nodes. Virtual nodes always come first; load balancing compares load ratio, then onlineUsers, then ranking. Drag-and-drop on the nodes page overwrites this value.
nodes.lbDragHint: Load balancing is active — drag sets tiebreaker priority when nodes have equal load
nodes.customConfigHint: During synchronization, replaces generation only when longer than 50 characters and containing listen: plus acme: or tls:. Short input falls back to generation; initial Auto Setup does not use it.
nodes.customConfigFormat: YAML format. Use 'Generate' button to fill with base config.
nodes.cascadeRoleHint: Defines the node's role in the cascade topology. Bridge nodes are hidden from user subscriptions.
nodes.rolePortal: Accepts clients and tunnels traffic through the cascade
nodes.roleBridge: Internet exit point, hidden from user subscriptions
nodes.roleRelay: Intermediate hop, forwards traffic further down the chain
nodes.countryHint: Country code for grouping on the network map
nodes.bridgeNodeHint: Bridge nodes are NOT visible in user subscriptions. Auto Setup will only install Xray (no Agent, no Reality). The actual bridge config is deployed when you create a cascade link.
nodes.portalNodeHint: Portal node — users connect here. Auto Setup works as usual (Xray + Agent + Reality). After setup, create a cascade link to connect to a Bridge node.
nodes.activeToggleError: Failed to update the node state
nodes.autoSetupConfirm:
Setup node automatically via SSH?

This will:
• Install Hysteria (if not installed)
• Generate certificate
• Upload configuration
• Setup port hopping
• Restart service
nodes.autoSetupConfirmXray:
Setup node automatically via SSH?

This will:
• Install Xray-core (latest version)
• Generate Reality keys (if needed)
• Install CC Agent (no-SSH management)
• Configure firewall
• Start services
nodes.setupRunning: Setup in progress... This may take 1-2 minutes.
nodes.cronConflictReload: Crontab changed on the node. Reload crontab before saving.
nodes.cronEmptyVirtualTitle: Cron is unavailable for virtual nodes
nodes.cronEmptyVirtualDesc: Virtual nodes aggregate other nodes in the topology, so there is no server to connect to and no remote cron to manage.
nodes.cronEmptySshDesc: Remote cron management needs SSH access to the node. Configure a username with a password or private key in the node settings to continue.
nodes.cronEmptySshStep1Desc: Use the button below to open this node's edit page.
nodes.cronEmptySshStep2Desc: Scroll to the Management section and provide a username plus a password or a private key.
nodes.cronEmptySshStep3Desc: After saving, return to the Cron section.
nodes.configHint: Copy this config to /etc/hysteria/config.yaml on the server:
nodes.loadConfigConfirm: Load current config from node via SSH?
nodes.confirmDeleteFull: Are you sure you want to delete this node?
nodes.ipAlreadyExists: A node with this IP already exists
nodes.ipTypeConflict: A {protocol} node with this IP already exists
nodes.addPairedProtocol: Add second protocol on this server
nodes.cloneNodeHint: Open a create form with this config. IP, domain, SSH and secrets stay empty.
nodes.restartHint: Restart the Hysteria or Xray service on the server
nodes.siblingNodeDetected: SSH settings will sync automatically from the existing node.
nodes.siblingExistsHint: {protocol} node already exists at this IP — SSH credentials will be synced automatically.
nodes.nameAndIpRequired: Name and IP address are required
nodes.virtualSectionHint: A virtual node groups Hysteria, Xray, and CDN sources. Xray JSON and compatible HAPP/Incy profiles receive a balancer; URI and v2ray-json omit the virtual group. An observatory is added only for leastPing/leastLoad; sing-box receives urltest and Mihomo a proxy-group.
nodes.virtualSelectModeGroupHint: All active nodes from the selected group are picked up automatically.
nodes.virtualSourcesHint: Sources may be Hysteria, Xray, or CDN nodes. Celerity expands their inbounds into each subscription's group format; URI and v2ray-json omit the virtual group.
nodes.virtualNoCandidates: No source nodes available. Create a Hysteria, Xray, or CDN node first.
nodes.virtualSourceGroupHint: All active non-virtual nodes from this group will be balanced. Nodes added to the group later are picked up automatically.
nodes.virtualStrategyHint: Strategy for the Xray balancer. leastLoad/leastPing require an observatory. For sing-box and Mihomo, Celerity maps the virtual node to the available url-test/load-balance construct, so semantics may differ.
nodes.virtualStrategyRandomDesc: Picks a random source on each connection. No probes. Good when servers are equivalent.
nodes.virtualStrategyRoundRobinDesc: Cycles through sources. Even distribution, no quality awareness.
nodes.virtualStrategyLeastPingDesc: Picks the source with the lowest probed latency. Requires the observatory below.
nodes.virtualStrategyLeastLoadDesc: The most stable outbound according to Xray observation results. Requires burstObservatory.
nodes.virtualObservatoryHint: leastPing uses the regular observatory; leastLoad uses burstObservatory. Random and Round Robin do not create probes.
nodes.virtualObsDestinationHint: URL probed through every source outbound; it should return HTTP 204 quickly. Celerity defaults to http://www.gstatic.com/generate_204.
nodes.virtualObsConnectivityHint: leastLoad/burstObservatory only: after a destination failure, checks local connectivity directly so logs can clarify the cause. Empty disables this check.
nodes.virtualObsIntervalHint: For leastPing, the probe start interval; for leastLoad, the expected average interval per outbound. Smaller values increase probe frequency.
nodes.virtualObsTimeoutHint: Timeout for one leastLoad/burstObservatory probe. The leastPing profile does not use this setting.
nodes.virtualObsSamplingHint: leastLoad/burstObservatory only: recent results kept by Xray. Celerity explicitly defaults to 3; Xray's default when omitted is 10.
nodes.virtualFallbackToFirstHint: For Xray profiles, sets the first outbound as fallbackTag when observed sources are unavailable. Other formats do not use this setting.
nodes.virtualUrltestHint: Clients without an Xray balancer resolve this node with a latency test. Xray ignores these settings and uses the strategy above.
nodes.virtualToleranceHint: How much faster another source must be before switching. Lower values switch more eagerly.
nodes.virtualIdleTimeoutHint: Stop probing after this long without traffic (sing-box only). Empty = core default.
nodes.virtualInterruptExistingHint: sing-box only: closes inbound connections when the selected outbound changes. sing-box always interrupts internal connections; Xray and Mihomo do not receive this setting.
nodes.virtualNoStatus: Virtual nodes don't connect to a server — they aggregate other nodes
nodes.sectionObfuscationHint: Salamander turns packets into patternless bytes; experimental Gecko also fragments and pads QUIC handshake packets. The password must match on client and server. When enabled, the server is incompatible with standard QUIC and is no longer a regular HTTP/3 server.
nodes.hopIntervalHint: Fixed interval for switching the client port. It only applies to an address with a port range; Hysteria uses 30s when omitted. Celerity accepts values of at least 5s.
nodes.acmeAdvancedHelp: Panel-only switch for extra challenge, listen host, alternate port, and DNS provider fields. ACME works with this block off; without a node domain, the entire section is ignored.
nodes.xrayListenHint: IPv4 or IPv6 interface address for Xray. 0.0.0.0 listens on all IPv4 interfaces; 127.0.0.1 accepts only local connections. Although Xray supports Unix sockets, this form accepts IP addresses only.
nodes.acmeEmailHelp: Hysteria ACME account email. When blank, Celerity sends acme@<node domain>.
nodes.acmeCaHelp: Certificate authority for ACME. Hysteria supports letsencrypt and zerossl.
nodes.acmeListenHostHelp: Local IP address, without a port, that accepts ACME validation. Default 0.0.0.0 listens on all IPv4 interfaces.
nodes.acmeTypeHelp: Domain validation method: HTTP-01, TLS-ALPN-01, or DNS-01. An empty value omits type and leaves the choice to Hysteria.
nodes.acmeHttpAltPortHelp: Local HTTP-01 port instead of 80. Public validation still reaches port 80, so port forwarding or an HTTP reverse proxy is required.
nodes.acmeTlsAltPortHelp: Local TLS-ALPN-01 port instead of 443. Public validation still reaches 443, so port forwarding or a TLS reverse proxy is required.
nodes.acmeDnsProviderHint: Available provider names are listed in ACME DNS config docs.
nodes.acmeDnsConfigHint: Raw JSON object for provider-specific credentials/options.
nodes.sectionMasqueradeHint: How Hysteria answers ordinary HTTP/3 requests: reverse-proxy a selected website or return a configured string. This makes the server resemble a normal HTTP/3 service.
nodes.masqueradeTypeHelp: proxy forwards requests to the selected website; string always returns the configured body, status, and headers. This Celerity form does not expose Hysteria's official file mode.
nodes.masqueradeProxyUrlHelp: Full website URL that Hysteria reverse-proxies for camouflage HTTP requests.
nodes.masqueradeProxyRewriteHostHelp: Replaces the original Host with the host from Proxy URL. Required when the target website selects its virtual host from this header.
nodes.masqueradeProxyInsecure: Disable TLS verification for the proxied website
nodes.masqueradeProxyInsecureHelp: Disables certificate verification for the HTTPS camouflage website, reducing security between the node and that website.
nodes.masqueradeStringContentHelp: Body of every camouflage HTTP response in string mode.
nodes.masqueradeStringStatusCodeHelp: HTTP status for string-mode camouflage responses. Hysteria defaults to 200; Celerity initially fills in 503.
nodes.masqueradeStringHeadersHint: One header per line: key: value
nodes.masqueradeListenHttpHelp: Optional TCP address for ordinary HTTP camouflage, such as :80. It does not change the main QUIC/UDP listener.
nodes.masqueradeListenHttpsHelp: Optional TCP address for HTTPS camouflage, such as :443. It uses the same certificate as the Hysteria server.
nodes.masqueradeForceHttpsHelp: Redirects every request from listenHTTP to HTTPS. It only matters when HTTP/HTTPS camouflage listeners are configured.
nodes.sectionBandwidthHint: Server-side upload/download limits and client limit policy.
nodes.sectionSpeedTestHint: Enables Hysteria's built-in speed test; its traffic is counted by stats and follows Bandwidth limits.
nodes.sectionUdpHint: UDP forwarding behavior and idle timeout.
nodes.sniffAdvancedHelp: Exposes custom timeout, rewriteDomain, and port lists. The separate switch above controls sniffing itself; when this block is off, Celerity keeps its default values.
nodes.quicAdvancedHelp: Exposes QUIC parameter overrides. QUIC operates independently of this switch; when it is off, Celerity restores and writes its own defaults.
nodes.bandwidthEnableHelp: Enables server bandwidth limits and the ignoreClientBandwidth policy. Celerity clears those settings when switched off.
nodes.udpOptionsHelp: Enables custom disableUDP and udpIdleTimeout values. Celerity resets both when switched off.
nodes.bandwidthUpHelp: Limit sent by the server per client—the client's download. It currently applies only to a direction using Brutal. Use units such as 100 mbps; empty means no server limit.
nodes.bandwidthDownHelp: Limit received by the server per client—the client's upload. It currently applies only to a direction using Brutal. Use a value with units; empty means no server limit.
nodes.ignoreClientBandwidthHelp: Ignores client bandwidth hints. Brutal is not selected in either direction, and each endpoint uses its own locally configured non-Brutal congestion controller.
nodes.speedTestHelp: Enables Hysteria's built-in upload/download test server. Test traffic follows Bandwidth limits and is counted by the Traffic Stats API.
nodes.disableUdpHelp: Disables client UDP forwarding completely; only TCP connections remain available through the proxy.
nodes.udpIdleTimeoutHelp: How long the server keeps a local UDP port for an inactive UDP session, similar to a NAT UDP session timeout.
nodes.sectionSniffQuicHint: Advanced options from Full Server Config.
nodes.sniffEnableHelp: Uses DPI to extract a domain from HTTP Host, TLS SNI, or QUIC SNI when a client request contains only an IP, allowing domain ACL rules to match.
nodes.sniffRewriteDomain: Rewrite requests that are already domain-based
nodes.sniffRewriteDomainHelp: Also sniffs requests where the client already supplied a domain and replaces it with the detected domain.
nodes.sniffTimeoutHelp: Maximum time to identify the protocol and domain. After it expires, the server connects to the original address.
nodes.sniffPortsHint: Same format as Port Hopping: comma-separated ports/ranges, or `all`.
nodes.quicInitStreamReceiveWindowHelp: Initial unread-data allowance for one incoming QUIC stream, in bytes. Celerity writes 8388608 by default.
nodes.quicMaxStreamReceiveWindowHelp: Maximum receive window for one stream. Celerity prevents it from being lower than the initial value.
nodes.quicInitConnReceiveWindowHelp: Initial aggregate unread-data allowance for all streams in one QUIC connection, in bytes. Celerity writes 20971520 by default.
nodes.quicMaxConnReceiveWindowHelp: Maximum aggregate receive window for a QUIC connection. Celerity keeps it at least as large as the initial value; Hysteria recommends a stream-to-connection ratio near 2:5.
nodes.quicMaxIdleTimeoutHelp: How long the server considers a client connected with no activity. Celerity writes 60s by default.
nodes.quicMaxIncomingStreamsHelp: Maximum number of concurrently open incoming QUIC streams per connection. Celerity writes 256 by default.
nodes.quicDisablePathMtuDiscoveryHelp: Prevents QUIC from discovering the largest packet size along the network path. Leave off unless PMTU discovery causes problems.
nodes.sectionResolverHint: DNS resolver settings used by the server.
nodes.resolverEnabledHelp: Sets the DNS server Hysteria uses to resolve domains in client requests. When disabled, the node's system resolver is used.
nodes.resolverTypeHelp: Transport for server DNS queries: plain UDP/TCP, DNS over TLS, or DNS over HTTPS.
nodes.resolverAddrHelp: DNS server address in host:port form for the selected transport.
nodes.resolverTimeoutHelp: Maximum time to wait for a DNS resolver response.
nodes.resolverSniHelp: TLS server name for tls and https resolver types. When TLS verification is enabled, it must match the DNS server certificate.
nodes.resolverInsecureHelp: Disables resolver certificate verification for tls/https. Use only with a trusted self-signed resolver.
nodes.sectionAclHint: Use either `inline` or `file` (not both). GeoIP/GeoSite options are optional.
nodes.aclEnableHelp: When disabled, Celerity omits ACL from the Hysteria config and locks the separate Outbounds / ACL editor for this node.
nodes.aclTypeHelp: Rule source: inline stores rules in the config, while file points to a file on the node. Hysteria accepts only one form.
nodes.aclFileHelp: Path to an existing ACL file on the node. Celerity does not create that file's contents.
nodes.aclInlineRulesHint: One rule per line. Celerity replaces an empty field with reject(geoip:cn) and reject(geoip:private).
nodes.aclGeoipHelp: Optional GeoIP dat-file path. When omitted, Hysteria downloads the database at startup if a rule needs it.
nodes.aclGeositeHelp: Optional GeoSite dat-file path. When omitted, Hysteria downloads the database at startup if a rule needs it.
nodes.aclGeoUpdateIntervalHelp: Refresh interval for automatically downloaded GeoIP/GeoSite data; Hysteria documents 168h as the default. A server restart is currently required for another download.
nodes.aclRulesEditorHint: Inline ACL rules are edited on the
nodes.domainHintHysteria: If set — TLS certificate will be issued automatically (ACME). Also used in subscription URLs instead of IP.
nodes.sniHintHysteria: Custom client SNI without an ACME domain. The panel publishes it to clients, disables server sniGuard, and enables certificate verification bypass. It is ignored when a domain is set.
nodes.outboundsAclLockedDisabled: Outbounds ACL editor is unavailable because ACL is disabled for this node.
nodes.hintDomain: Domain for SNI and ACME certificates
nodes.hintPortRange: UDP port range for port hopping (e.g., 20000-50000)
nodes.hintMaxOnline: 0 = unlimited. Overload hiding depends on the global hideOverloaded setting.
nodes.hintRanking: Virtual nodes come first; real-node order depends on load balancing and ranking.
nodes.sshNotConfigured: SSH not configured. Auto-setup and terminal require SSH credentials.
nodes.xrayTransportHelp: How the VLESS stream is carried; client and server must use compatible transports. REALITY supports TCP/RAW, XHTTP and gRPC, but not WebSocket.
nodes.xraySecurityHelp: Transport security: REALITY imitates the selected target's TLS without a separate node certificate; TLS uses a certificate; None does not encrypt the transport and is intended for a trusted network or an external TLS terminator.
nodes.xrayFingerprintHint: Client-side uTLS fingerprint for a Reality/TLS handshake; it is not added to the server Xray config.
nodes.xrayFingerprintHelp: Celerity publishes this client-side uTLS fingerprint in subscriptions; it does not change the server TLS configuration. In pool mode, one selected fingerprint is chosen when the subscription is rendered and stays fixed until its cache refreshes.
nodes.xrayFingerprintPoolHint: One selected fingerprint is chosen when the subscription is rendered and remains fixed until its cache refreshes.
nodes.xrayFingerprintModePoolHint: Pick several; one is chosen when the subscription is rendered and remains fixed until its cache refreshes.
nodes.xrayAlpnHint: Comma-separated TLS ALPN list. gRPC requires h2; WebSocket normally uses http/1.1. Order matters. When blank, Celerity gives the server h2,http/1.1 but does not publish an explicit client ALPN.
nodes.xrayFlowHint: Celerity applies XTLS Vision only to TCP + REALITY/TLS. The default is xtls-rprx-vision; a blank TCP field does not disable Vision because the generator restores that default. WebSocket, gRPC, and XHTTP ignore this field.
nodes.xrayRealityDestHint: REALITY target in fallback-destination form, usually host:port: its TLS appearance is used as camouflage and connections that fail verification are forwarded to it.
nodes.xrayRealitySniHint: Comma-separated client serverNames accepted by REALITY, without wildcards. Every name must be accepted by the target certificate. The server receives the full list, but Celerity publishes only the first name to clients.
nodes.sniScanHint: Scans the node IP's /24 for TLS 1.3 and H2 hosts whose DNS is confirmed in that subnet. These are preliminary candidates; verify REALITY target suitability separately.
nodes.sniScanIpHelp: IPv4 address whose /24 subnet will be scanned. The fill button uses the current node IP.
nodes.sniScanPortHelp: TLS port used to test candidates. The Apply button currently always writes port 443 to the REALITY target, even when another port was scanned.
nodes.sniScanThreadsHelp: Concurrent address checks, from 1 to 200. Higher values scan faster but increase network and CPU load.
nodes.sniScanTimeoutHelp: Timeout for checking one address, from 2 to 30 seconds.
nodes.sniScanNoResults: No suitable SNI hosts found in this subnet.
nodes.sniScanNeighborHint: DNS confirmed in the same /24; verify the REALITY target separately
nodes.sniScanOtherHint: The domain resolves outside the scanned /24; this is not a same-subnet candidate
nodes.xrayPrivateKeyHelp: Server-side REALITY X25519 private key. Celerity sends it only to the inbound; clients receive the public key from the adjacent field. Manually entered key pairs are not checked for correspondence.
nodes.xrayPublicKeyHelp: Client-side REALITY X25519 public key matching the inbound private key. It is not used by the server inbound; Celerity publishes it to clients and does not verify manually entered key pairs.
nodes.xrayShortIdsHint: Allowed client shortIds: comma-separated hexadecimal strings with an even length from 0 to 16 characters. An empty string is valid; Celerity publishes the first non-empty item to clients. The panel does not currently validate manually entered values.
nodes.xraySpiderXHint: Optional initial path and query for the client-side REALITY spider; it must start with /. Celerity stores one value per inbound and publishes it to clients; blank keeps the core default.
nodes.xrayWsPathHelp: The HTTP Upgrade path for WebSocket. Default: /. Client, server and reverse proxy must route a compatible path.
nodes.xrayWsHostHint: HTTP Host sent by the client and checked by the inbound when its server value is non-empty. With TLS, Celerity gives clients the TLS domain when this field is blank; an explicit value is mainly needed for a CDN or reverse proxy.
nodes.xrayGrpcServiceHelp: The gRPC service name must match on client and server. The normal path is /<serviceName>/Tun; a leading / selects Xray custom-path syntax. The transport runs over HTTP/2, and Caddy Front rejects variants containing |.
nodes.xrayXhttpHostHint: Optional Host override for a CDN or reverse proxy. Leave empty to derive it from the TLS server name or connection address.
nodes.xrayXhttpModeHint: auto: normally packet-up; with REALITY, stream-one; with REALITY + downloadSettings, stream-up.
nodes.xrayXhttpTuningHint: Optional. Ranges are written as "min-max" or a single number; leave empty to keep Xray defaults. Client cores differ in which advanced XHTTP keys they support.
nodes.xrayXhttpPathHelp: The base XHTTP URL path. Default: /. The client may append session/sequence segments and the server checks the prefix. Celerity's Caddy front requires a path other than /; front paths cannot be equal or one path's parent prefix.
nodes.xrayXhttpHostHelp: The HTTP Host sent by the client and checked by the server when set. If empty, the client derives it from the TLS server name or connection address. Mainly used with CDNs and reverse proxies.
nodes.xrayXhttpModeHelp: On the current Xray client, auto selects packet-up normally, stream-one with REALITY, or stream-up with REALITY plus downloadSettings. packet-up splits uploads into requests; stream-up uses a separate upload stream; stream-one uses one bidirectional request. On the server, auto accepts all three.
nodes.xrayXhttpPaddingHint: Random padding in client requests and, except for query placement, server responses. Default 100-1000. Celerity widens the server range to keep default clients compatible.
nodes.xrayXhttpPaddingHelp: Random padding size. Default: 100-1000 bytes. Current Xray requires both range bounds to be greater than 0. The client request range must fit within the server range; query placement cannot add padding to responses.
nodes.xrayXhttpMaxPostHint: Upload split threshold in packet-up mode. Default 1000000. The node accepts at least the default, so a smaller value here applies only to clients that read it.
nodes.xrayXhttpMaxPostHelp: Limits one packet-up upload request. Default: 1000000 bytes. The server's upper bound must be at least the client's upper bound.
nodes.xrayXhttpXmuxConcurrencyHelp: Maximum simultaneous proxy streams over one underlying connection. 0 means unlimited. This option is client-side only.
nodes.xrayXhttpXmuxRequestsHelp: Limits HTTP requests over one connection's lifetime. 0 means unlimited. When every XMUX field is empty, current Xray applies a default bundle that includes 600-900.
nodes.xrayXhttpXmuxReusableSecsHelp: After this time the connection stops accepting new requests and closes when active requests finish. 0 means unlimited; Xray's default bundle uses 1800-3000 seconds.
nodes.xrayXhttpXmuxHint: Client-side only. Leaving all XMUX fields empty keeps Xray's default bundle: maxConnections 3, 600-900 requests and 1800-3000 reusable seconds. Setting any XMUX field disables that bundle; omitted XMUX limits become 0.
nodes.xrayXhttpNoGrpcHeader: Do not send the gRPC header
nodes.xrayXhttpNoGrpcHeaderHint: In stream-up/stream-one the client marks requests as gRPC so CDNs do not buffer the response. Enable this option only if the proxy in front rejects that content type.
nodes.xrayXhttpNoGrpcHeaderHelp: Applies to stream-up and stream-one. By default the client sends Content-Type: application/grpc so intermediate proxies do not buffer the stream.
nodes.xrayXhttpUploadMethodHelp: HTTP method used by the client for upload requests. Default: POST. GET requires explicit packet-up mode and cannot carry data in the body.
nodes.xrayXhttpDataPlacementHelp: Where packet-up carries payload data. With the empty/default setting, the client sends body data while the server accepts header, cookie and body data. Explicit header or cookie requires packet-up and a matching key.
nodes.xrayXhttpDataKeyHelp: Name used for data fragments in headers or cookies; it must match on both sides. Xray defaults: X-Data for header and x_data for cookie.
nodes.xrayXhttpChunkSizeHelp: Fragment size for packet-up over headers or cookies. Defaults: 3000-4000 for header and 2048-3072 for cookie; minimum 64 bytes.
nodes.xrayXhttpMinPostIntervalHelp: Minimum client interval between packet-up requests. Default: 30 ms per proxy connection. A single value of 0 is normalized back to the 30 ms default.
nodes.xrayXhttpMaxHeaderBytesHelp: Request-header limit on Xray's HTTP/1.1 and H2 listener. Default: 8192 bytes; 0 keeps the default. CDN and reverse-proxy limits are separate.
nodes.xrayXhttpPaddingPlacementHelp: Used only when padding obfuscation is enabled. Default: queryInHeader. In current Xray, query adds padding to requests but cannot add it to responses.
nodes.xrayXhttpPaddingKeyHelp: Parameter or cookie name for query, cookie, and queryInHeader padding. Default: x_padding. It must match on the client and server.
nodes.xrayXhttpPaddingMethodHelp: Padding content format when obfuscation is enabled: repeat-x by default, or tokenish. Both sides must use the same method.
nodes.xrayXhttpPaddingHeaderHelp: HTTP header name for header or queryInHeader placement. With obfuscation enabled, the default is X-Padding.
nodes.xrayXhttpSessionTableHelp: Client-side alphabet used to generate session IDs. Empty/Default generates UUID. Current Xray has no uuid preset: the literal uuid is a custom four-character alphabet and requires a valid length.
nodes.xrayXhttpSessionLengthHelp: Session ID length for a custom alphabet. Accepts a number or range; without an alphabet, Xray uses UUID.
nodes.xrayXhttpPaddingObfsHelp: Enables custom padding placement, key, header and method. When off, client requests use x_padding in the Referer URL and server responses use X-Padding.
nodes.xrayXhttpSessionPlacementHelp: Where to carry the session ID in packet-up and stream-up. Default: path. stream-one does not use a separate session ID.
nodes.xrayXhttpSessionKeyHelp: Session ID name for query, header, or cookie; unused with path. Defaults: X-Session for header and x_session for query/cookie.
nodes.xrayXhttpSeqPlacementHelp: Where to carry the part number in packet-up. Default: path. Streaming modes do not use sequence numbers.
nodes.xrayXhttpSeqKeyHelp: Sequence name for query, header, or cookie; unused with path. Defaults: X-Seq for header and x_seq for query/cookie.
nodes.cdnDesc: Publish an Xray inbound through CDN edges
nodes.cdnSectionHint: Choose one Xray origin inbound. Each enabled edge becomes a separate subscription entry.
nodes.cdnOriginNodeHelp: The active Xray node that serves users of this CDN node. Celerity synchronizes those users to the origin even when the origin itself is not published to their groups.
nodes.cdnOriginInboundHelp: The origin inbound to publish. WebSocket, gRPC and XHTTP are supported with TLS or no transport security; REALITY is incompatible with a CDN that terminates TLS.
nodes.cdnTransportUnsupported: transport is not supported by CDN
nodes.cdnRealityUnsupported: REALITY cannot be used behind a CDN
nodes.cdnMihomoExcluded: Mihomo excluded: GET uplink is unsupported
nodes.cdnFingerprintHelp: Client-side uTLS fingerprint for connecting to the CDN. In pool mode, Celerity distributes the selected fingerprints across published edges from a random offset; values repeat only when there are more edges than fingerprints.
nodes.cdnFingerprintPoolHint: Fingerprints are assigned across edges from a random offset; repeats are unavoidable when there are more edges than pool values.
nodes.frontHint: Caddy accepts connections on the public port, serves the decoy site at /, and routes requests to the selected inbounds.
nodes.frontDisclaimerTitle: Requires a domain, SSH and a separate VPS
nodes.frontDisclaimerMessage: Caddy accepts TLS for the node domain and forwards requests to selected inbounds on 127.0.0.1. The domain is the public address and SNI. It may resolve to a proxy/CDN only if that service forwards the selected transport and public port; with ACME, certificate validation must also reach Caddy. Celerity does not verify this in advance. Use ACME or Manual PEM — the panel certificate is not supported. WebSocket, gRPC and XHTTP are available. Celerity programmatically forbids Front on the panel VPS regardless of the selected public port.
nodes.frontPublicPortHint: The port clients connect to. Caddy listens here instead of the inbounds.
nodes.frontInboundsHint: Each one keeps its own path and gets a loopback port assigned on save. Paths cannot be /, equal one another, or be a prefix of another front path.
nodes.frontSitePending: selected, {bytes} bytes — uploaded when the node is saved
nodes.frontSiteUploadFailed: Node created, but the decoy page upload failed: {error}
nodes.frontSiteHint: Served on paths outside the inbounds. nginx mode uses a static welcome-page copy without running nginx; custom accepts a non-empty file up to 262144 bytes. Celerity neither validates the HTML nor sanitizes its contents.
nodes.frontApplyHint: Installs Caddy if needed, validates the config, and runs local Caddy/upstream smoke tests through 127.0.0.1. External reachability is not checked; selected inbounds stay hidden from subscriptions until Apply succeeds.
nodes.frontNoCandidates: No suitable inbounds: the front can only serve WebSocket, gRPC and XHTTP.
nodes.cdnDomainHint: Optional when edge addresses are entered manually. Used for DNS discovery and as the direct subscription address when the edge list is empty.
nodes.cdnResolvedSources: Found {found} address(es); added {count} new. DNS sources checked: {sources}/{total}.
nodes.cdnPathMustExtend: Must start with {prefix} or be exactly the origin path.
nodes.cdnPathMustMatchOrigin: Leave empty or enter exactly {path}. A longer path prevents sessions from working because their identifiers are carried in the path.
nodes.cdnPathMustEqual: A WebSocket origin matches its path exactly — use {path} or leave this empty.
nodes.cdnPathUnsupported: The client path applies to XHTTP and WebSocket origins only.
nodes.cdnClientPortHelp: The public CDN port clients connect to. It does not change the inbound port on the origin.
nodes.cdnEdgesHint: Up to 32 addresses. Every enabled edge becomes a separate subscription entry; without edges, one entry uses the public CDN domain.
nodes.cdnEdgeAddressHelp: The public address the client connects to. With TLS, the certificate is still verified against SNI rather than this IP or hostname.
nodes.cdnClientPathHint: XHTTP: must equal the origin path while the session or sequence marker stays in the path (the default) — move them to a query, header or cookie to publish a longer path. WebSocket: must be empty or exactly the origin path.
nodes.cdnSniHelp: The server name in TLS ClientHello and the name used to verify the CDN certificate. Celerity defaults it to the public CDN domain; it is required and must be a valid hostname.
nodes.cdnHostHelp: The HTTP Host/authority sent through the CDN or reverse proxy. It defaults to the public domain, then SNI, and may differ from the edge address.
nodes.cdnAlpnHelp: The ALPN protocols offered by the client to the CDN. They must match the transport and CDN capabilities; their order is preserved in subscriptions.
nodes.cdnXhttpModeHelp: Optional client-side XHTTP mode override. The origin keeps its upload method and framing; Celerity rejects an incompatible combination when saving.
nodes.cdnAllowInsecure: Unavailable: Celerity always requires a verifiable CDN certificate
nodes.xrayTlsSourceScopeHint: One certificate strategy per node — applies to every TLS inbound (main and extras).
nodes.xrayTlsSourcePanelHint: Embeds the PANEL_DOMAIN certificate from panel storage; clients receive PANEL_DOMAIN as TLS SNI and HTTP Host. PANEL_DOMAIN and readable cert/key files are required. Caddy Front does not support this source.
nodes.xrayTlsSourceAcmeHint: For a direct TLS inbound, Auto Setup uses acme.sh with HTTP-01; when Caddy Front is enabled, Caddy manages the public certificate. In both cases, domain DNS must point to the node.
nodes.xrayTlsAcmeInfoLine: For a direct TLS inbound, ensure the DNS A record points to the node and port 80 is reachable: Auto Setup installs acme.sh and renewal cron. For Caddy Front, Caddy manages ACME.
nodes.xrayTlsAcmeEmailHint: Used to register the ACME account. Leave empty to fall back to the panel-wide ACME_EMAIL env var.
nodes.xrayTlsSourceManualHint: Use a separate domain for the node and paste a full certificate chain and private key. The PEM is inlined into the node config.
nodes.xrayTlsSourceSelfSignedHint: Auto Setup creates a self-signed certificate if certificate files do not yet exist and keeps them on the node. Clients must enable allowInsecure — testing only.
nodes.xrayTlsPanelDomainUnset: PANEL_DOMAIN is not set — the Panel domain source is unavailable
nodes.xrayTlsPanelInfoLine: The panel certificate is sent to the node during synchronization; separate certificate files are not required on the node.
nodes.xrayTlsManualDomainHint: Set the node domain in the Network section above (it doubles as the TLS server name).
nodes.xrayTlsSelfSignedWarning: Self-signed certificates are easy to fingerprint and require allowInsecure on every client.
nodes.xrayTlsSelfSignedHint: Use a real Panel, ACME, or Manual certificate for production.
nodes.xrayManualCertHint: Paste the full chain: leaf certificate followed by intermediates, each in its own BEGIN/END block.
nodes.xrayManualKeyHint: Paste a PKCS8, EC, or RSA private key. After saving, the field is not returned to the form and is shown as ***SET***.
nodes.xrayManualKeyMaskedHint: A private key is already saved. Paste a new PEM block to replace it, or leave ***SET*** unchanged.
nodes.xrayPemInvalid: Not a valid PEM block — check BEGIN/END markers
nodes.domainHintXrayManual: Domain used as the TLS server name and as the Host header for ws/xhttp transports.
nodes.xrayApiPortHint: Local port for management API (not public, default 61000)
nodes.xrayFallbackDestHint: Where to redirect non-VLESS traffic, including active probes. In this form use a port (8080), host:port (127.0.0.1:8080), or [v6]:port. Do not use unix:/path: current Xray expects an absolute socket path, which Celerity's validator does not yet accept. TCP+TLS only; REALITY uses its own target.
nodes.xrayExtraInboundsHint: Run VLESS inbounds on different ports and transports. Every available inbound is published separately; a Front-selected inbound appears only after a successful Apply. TLS strategy is shared by the node.
nodes.xrayRemoveInboundConfirm: Remove this inbound? Connected clients on this port will be disconnected on the next sync.
nodes.xrayInboundLabelHelp: Human-readable label for the extra inbound. Celerity normally publishes it as "Node (label)"; with Unique name enabled and a non-empty label, only the label is used.
nodes.xrayInboundUniqueNameHint: When enabled with a non-empty label, the subscription uses just the label instead of "Node name (label)".
nodes.xrayInboundTagHelp: Unique internal Xray tag used for routing and the API. It must differ from every other inbound tag on this node.
nodes.xrayInboundPortHelp: Port for the extra VLESS inbound and, without Front, the client connection port. It must be free and differ from other inbounds and the Xray API; Caddy Front moves a selected inbound to an internal loopback port.

nodes.xrayInboundTagConflict: This tag is already used by another inbound
nodes.agentOutdatedMessage: Extra inbounds are configured, but the agent on this node is older than 1.2.0 — it cannot manage users on the additional inbounds. Re-run the node setup from the management section to upgrade the agent.
nodes.agentUpdateAvailableMessage: This node runs an agent older than 1.3.0. Users may lose connectivity after Xray restarts. Update the agent from the Management section or through the broadcast terminal.

settings.happAnnounceHint: Short message shown to users inside the app (max 200 characters). Non-ASCII text (e.g. Cyrillic) is encoded automatically.
settings.softBlockDesc: Return a subscription containing informational entries with your message instead of an error. Works with all client applications.
settings.softBlockEnableHint: When off, invalid subscriptions return a plain 403 (legacy behavior).

settings.happHwidIntro: Limit how many physical devices a single subscription can be used on, by the x-hwid header sent by the client. Enforced at subscription fetch.

settings.happHwidExplainStrict: Works like Soft mode, but clients without the x-hwid header receive a subscription containing “No HWID support” informational entries instead of available servers.
settings.happHwidExplainSoftBlock: When the device limit is exceeded, the client receives a subscription containing “Limit reached” informational entries instead of available servers. HAPP also displays an in-app message. The response remains compatible with VPN clients.

settings.happHwidMaxDevicesRemarkHint: Shown when the device limit is reached. Each non-empty line appears as a separate informational entry. Up to 12 lines, 32 characters per line.
settings.happHwidAnnounceHint: Sent to HAPP with the informational entry and shown as an in-app message. Up to 300 characters; non-ASCII characters are Base64-encoded.
settings.happPingTypeHint: How the app measures server latency.
settings.happPingUrlHint: URL used for proxy ping check. Only applies when ping method is Via Proxy.

settings.routingDesc: Configure which websites and services your users access directly (bypassing VPN) and which go through the VPN tunnel.
settings.routingEnabledHint: When disabled, subscriptions are generated without routing rules — all traffic goes through VPN.
settings.routingHowItWorksDesc:
Routing rules are embedded into subscription configs delivered to VPN clients. When a user opens a website or app, the client checks the destination against these rules:
• direct — traffic goes directly, bypassing the VPN (e.g. local banking, government services).
• block — traffic is dropped (e.g. ads, trackers).
• Everything else goes through the VPN tunnel as usual.

Rules also configure Split DNS: domains matching direct rules are resolved via the domestic DNS server, while all other queries go through the encrypted remote DNS.
settings.routingPresetsHint: Presets are additive — click multiple presets to combine them. For example, "Bypass RU" + "Block Ads" will add both rule sets. Duplicate rules are skipped automatically.
settings.routingRulesHint: Rules are applied top to bottom. First match wins. Disabled rules are skipped. Note: sing-box clients only accept country codes for geoip (ru, cn); provider lists such as geoip:telegram exist in Xray and Clash only and are dropped for sing-box.
settings.routingNoRules: No rules yet. Add manually or pick a preset above.
settings.routingDnsHint: Domains matching "direct" rules are resolved via the domestic DNS. Everything else is resolved through the remote (encrypted) DNS via proxy tunnel.
settings.routingDnsDomesticHint: Plain UDP DNS for direct domains (e.g. Yandex DNS: 77.88.8.8)
settings.routingDnsRemoteHint: Encrypted DNS for proxied traffic (e.g. Cloudflare DoT: tls://1.1.1.1)
settings.routingClientSupportDesc:
Full support: HAPP (native routing protocol), Clash Meta / Stash (YAML rules).
Partial support: Hiddify / SFA / NekoBox (sing-box JSON — some clients may override rules with their own templates).
No support: v2rayNG, Streisand, Shadowrocket — these clients use URI subscriptions which cannot carry routing rules. Users need to configure routing manually.

network.modeReverseHint: Bridge initiates tunnel to Portal. Bridge can be behind NAT.
network.modeForwardHint: Portal connects to Bridge directly. All nodes need public IP.
network.confirmDeployChain: Deploy entire chain? This will sync all connected nodes in the correct order.

wizard.title: Setup Wizard
wizard.subtitle: Prepare the panel, the first nodes, and the initial access bundle in one guided flow.
wizard.scenarioHint: Select the deployment model that best matches your infrastructure. This only prepares the initial layout, and you can still add or change nodes later.
wizard.selfHostDesc: Install Hysteria 2 and / or Xray on the same server as the panel and prepare the starter access layout immediately.
wizard.remoteDesc: Use the panel as a control plane for proxy nodes running on separate VPS or dedicated servers.
wizard.selfHostHint: Choose the protocols to deploy, provide SSH access to the target server, and the wizard will prepare the starter group and first user automatically.
wizard.starterBundleDesc: The wizard will create a starter server group, attach the new nodes to it, and prepare the first VPN user admin so the subscription layout is ready immediately after deployment.
wizard.hysteriaChoiceDesc: High-performance UDP transport with QUIC and port hopping support.
wizard.xrayChoiceDesc: TCP transport with REALITY camouflage and management through the built-in agent.
wizard.hyDomainHint: Uses the panel domain. Hysteria shares the panel TLS certificate.
wizard.xrayPortHint: Port 443/tcp is used by the panel (Caddy). Xray defaults to 8443.
wizard.sshAccess: SSH access to the target server
wizard.sshAccessHint: Provide an address the panel can reach over SSH. Root access is recommended for unattended installation.
wizard.installing: Provisioning nodes, preparing starter access, and validating services. Please wait...
wizard.installPartial: Provisioning finished with errors. Fix the issue and retry setup, or continue manually.
wizard.streamError: Connection lost. Refresh to check status.
wizard.noProtocolSelected: Please select at least one protocol.
wizard.tooManyRequests: Too many requests. Try again later.
wizard.serverAddressRequired: Server IP or hostname is required
wizard.sshAuthRequired: SSH password or private key is required
wizard.credentialsDesc: Use this subscription link for the automatically prepared admin starter access.

migration.off: Legacy compatibility is OFF. Complete the wizard below to import users and arm the compat route.
migration.disableConfirm: Disable the Marzban compat route? Old links stop resolving until re-enabled.
migration.connectTitle: Connect to the source Marzban panel
migration.connectDesc: Provide the panel URL and the credentials of a sudo (or owning) admin. We never store these — they only live in this browser session until the import finishes.
migration.marzbanUrlHint: Include the protocol. Trailing slashes are stripped automatically.
migration.configureDesc: Choose which Celerity ServerGroup each Marzban admin's users land in, set the legacy subscription path, and paste the Marzban JWT secret so old links can be verified.
migration.pathHint: Must match the source panel's XRAY_SUBSCRIPTION_PATH. Default is sub. Reserved: api, panel, health, sse, docs, public, static.
migration.acceptSalt: Accept random URL salt (only if Marzban used XRAY_SUBSCRIPTION_URL_PREFIX with a *).
migration.jwtSecretPlaceholder: 64-char hex string from `SELECT secret_key FROM jwt;`
migration.jwtSecretHint: The command below runs inside the Marzban container and reads the secret through Marzban's own Python/SQLAlchemy layer. That makes it work with SQLite, MySQL, or any other database configured in the panel. Celerity stores the secret AES-encrypted.
migration.jwtSecretCommandTitle: Command to get the JWT secret
migration.jwtSecretCommandDesc: Run it on the server where Marzban is running. The command automatically finds the Marzban container by image or name.
migration.mappingDesc: Each Marzban admin's users join the chosen Celerity ServerGroup. The dropdown lists active groups only.
migration.fallbackGroup: Fallback ServerGroup (for users whose admin is unmapped)
migration.importVless: Re-use Marzban VLESS UUIDs (keeps Xray identity stable for users who already had VLESS).
migration.runDesc: Do not close this page or restart the panel until the import finishes; the operation will be interrupted.
migration.finalizeDesc: Imported users are already in Celerity. The last step enables the /{path}/{token} route so old subscription links keep working.
migration.activateSuccess: Compat route armed. Old links should resolve now.

probes.title: External probes
probes.subtitle: Diagnostic agents that connect to your nodes like a regular client and report the result.
probes.disabledBanner: External probes are disabled. Enable them in settings.
probes.settingsIntro: A probe is a separate application installed on your server. It receives a service subscription, starts sing-box, and connects to nodes like a regular client.
probes.enableHint: While disabled, the panel accepts neither probe enrollment nor reports.
probes.installHint: Run this command on the server you want to check from. The token is single-use and expires in 24 hours.
probes.blockedHint: Traffic limit reached, so the panel stopped serving its subscription. Reset the counter to continue without reinstalling.
probes.confirmRemove: Delete this probe together with its subscription and check history?
probes.scaleWarning: Probes times nodes times resources has grown large enough to load both the panel and the nodes noticeably.
probes.nodeSectionHint: What probes see when they connect to this node as a regular client. Every vantage point is shown separately, since a failure can also come from the probe's own uplink.
probes.sameHost: This probe runs on the node address, so its traffic never leaves the machine
probes.trafficLimitHint: Caps the hidden probe user. 0 means no limit.
probes.speedHint: Measurement spends real traffic on your nodes, so it is bounded per run and by a daily budget.
probes.speedEstimateLoad: A run pulls up to {size}. Every inbound is measured {runs} times a day, about {daily} of traffic from one probe.
probes.speedEstimateNoBudget: The daily budget covers {runs} runs, after which measurement pauses until the next day.
probes.speedEstimateCeiling: This size and time limit can measure up to {ceiling} Mbit/s. Anything faster fills the size cap first and is reported as "≥ {ceiling} Mbit/s" — raise the size to measure higher.
probes.targetsHint: One list for the whole panel: every resource is checked through every node. An unreachable resource usually means a geo-block or a blacklisted exit address.
probes.historyHint: Each segment is one check window. Ranges longer than 12 hours are shown as hourly rollups.
probes.historyEmpty: This probe has not reported any checks in the selected range.
probes.historyPending: Data will appear after the probe is installed.
probes.truncated: More data than fits: only the end of the period is shown.
